To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spatial resolution of PET detectors is improved when intercrystal scatter is accounted for, that continuous DOI information provides the most accurate spatial resolution and that the improvement is independent of the crystal size and the stopping power of the scintillator.
the impact of inter crystal crosstalk on spatial resolution is similar for discrete and continuous depth-of-interaction readout schemes, but that the continuous readout is less affected by crosstalk.
intercrystal crossovers are a significant source of degradation of spatial resolution in PET systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of intercrystal scatter on the spatial resolution and DOI information of whole body PET scanners.
the impact of inter crystal scatter on the spatial resolution and DOI information of whole body PET scanners using different readout schemes.
the impact of inter crystal crosstalk in the spatial resolution in PET detectors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the continuous DOI readout method is the best choice for a whole-body PET scanner with respect to spatial resolution and DOI information.
the intercrystal scatter has a minor impact on the spatial resolution for the investigated detector geometries.
the continuous readout is superior to discrete readout in terms of the full width at the tenth maximum, while both readout schemes provide similar results for the full widths at the half maximum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the continuous DOI readout is most resistant to intercrystal scatter, but the improvement in the spatial resolution is not significant.
the continuous DOI readout is the most robust approach against intercrystal scatter, and the discrete approach with two offset crystal layers is most sensitive to intercrystal scatter.
intercrystal scatter does not significantly impair the spatial resolution in the field of view, but it is a significant source of noise for the continuous approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the continuous readout approach is less sensitive to intercrystal scatter than the discrete approach.
the continuous approach is the most robust against intercrystal scatter.
the continuous approach provides better spatial resolution at the edge of the detector, while discrete approaches are better suited for detectors with a large number of crystals.
